title: Displacement stage division and characteristic analysis before failure of Tonglüshan tailings dam based on improved displacement tangent angle method
content:
by Qiao Liang, Li Xiaojing, Yang Yue, Li Zhiqiang, Liu Ya, Zhang Liyun, Xu Ning, Zhang Wei

Against the backdrop of the continuous development of the global mining industry, the number of tailings ponds is steadily increasing. The safety issues of tailings dams have emerged as significant potential hazards that affect the ecological environment, human life and property. Therefore, there is an urgent need for effective monitoring and analysis technologies. This study aims to utilize Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) technology to monitor the deformation of the Tonglüshan tailings dam, conduct an in-depth analysis of the causes and processes of its dam failure, and thereby explore practical methods for tailings dam safety monitoring. In the research methodology, the Small Baseline Subset Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (SBAS-InSAR) technology was employed to process 50 Sentinel-1A images. Moreover, by integrating the improved Displacement Tangent Angle Method (IDTAM), an easy approach was established to divide the deformation stages of the tailings dam. The research results are as follows. The deformation of the tailings dam exhibits four distinct stages. Evidently, precipitation plays a crucial role in promoting the dam's deformation. Additionally, significant correlative relationships have been identified among the deformations in different areas. Notably, the deformations in areas M1 and M2 are induced by different factors. Overall, this study has achieved significant findings. Firstly, it has successfully revealed a causal relationship between the dam failure of the Tonglüshan tailings dam and the collapse of the goaf in the northern part. Secondly, the improved Displacement Tangent Angle Method has proven to be a novel and valuable tool for analyzing the inversion results of InSAR technology. It holds great promise in the displacement monitoring and analysis of homogeneous slopes, providing a new perspective and method for similar engineering applications..
author: Qiao Liang
